          Man Utd vs Roma Prediction: Champions League Preview
        
      
                          
                      Nov 2, 2026
          
                      Jon O'Shea / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
We look ahead to Tuesday’s UEFA Champions League clash with our Man Utd vs Roma prediction and preview. Can United defy grim domestic form to beat visitors still undefeated in Serie A?
With their slump reaching new depths, Manchester United must try to pick up some precious Champions League points when free-scoring Roma visit Old Trafford on Tuesday.
It seems everyone is keen to have their say on Man Utd's latest crisis, but the stark facts speak for themselves.
Sparking talk of a relegation fight, the fallen giants have taken just seven points from nine Premier League games this season, failing to even score in four.
Dating back to mid-September, United are winless in nine across all competitions (D3 L6), and that's their longest such run for 42 years.
After Lisandro Martínez was dismissed for his second booking on Saturday, the Red Devils inevitably slumped to defeat at Chelsea, losing 2-0 at Stamford Bridge.
United's only wins this season have come against promoted Ipswich Town and Azerbaijan's Sabah, relative minnows in Champions League terms.
After the latter result got United off the mark in this season's UCL, they subsequently lost 2-0 to Atlético Madrid before being mauled by European newcomers Como.

Their dismal 4-1 defeat at Stadio Sinigaglia left United 21st in the Champions League table, and only the top 24 will progress beyond the league phase. Their next opponents are one point ahead in 15th.
Responding to a late implosion that cost them victory over Real Madrid, when they conceded three times in the final eight minutes to lose 4-3, Roma were emphatic winners last time out.
Admittedly, their visitors were only Slovan Bratislava, but two goals in either half secured the Giallorossi's first Champions League success since 2019.
Roma finally booked their return to the top table by finishing third in Serie A last term, capping an impressive first year for former Europa League winner Gian Piero Gasperini.
This season his team are unbeaten in Italy's top flight, claiming draws against potential title rivals Inter, Napoli and Como as well as seven wins.
Stretching back several months, Roma are undefeated in 17 top-flight fixtures, most recently smashing fast-sinking Udinese 5-2 on Saturday, when they went four goals up before half-time.
Now just behind old foes and surprise early leaders Lazio – and reigning champions Inter – Roma could be eyeing their first Scudetto for 26 years.
Roma have racked up 21 goals in six games since hanging on for a 0-0 draw with Como after Donyell Malen was sent off, and 14 different players have already scored in the current campaign.

However, history is not on Roma's side ahead of Tuesday's game. They've failed to win on any of their last 16 trips to England (D6 L10), and they've conceded in their last 32 Champions League away games, the longest run by any team in Europe's top competition.
Assuming United's misfiring attack can extend that to 33, the Giallorossi may need Malen to continue his red-hot form.

The Dutch forward is Serie A's top scorer for the calendar year, including eight goals from 10 games this term. In the Champions League, he's one of only five players with at least five goal involvements and has recorded the joint-most touches inside the opposition's box (26).
Malen's preferred partner is Paulo Dybala, with the pair striking up an intuitive understanding, but a familiar muscular problem could rule the Argentinian out.
